subject: BlueLantern volume slabs, per-token caps, and model premium breakdown
messages:
From: Alex Miller <alex@bluelantern.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Pricing ask — commit tiers, model premiums, embeddings pricing

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BlueLantern is excited about the latency profile on Redwood. Procurement asked me to get a formalized pricing proposal for hosted API consumption so we can model TCO. High level: we have a mix of chat (80%) and embedding (20%) traffic. Monthly token expectations: baseline 1.5B input tokens + 1.2B output tokens (mostly chat), embeddings are about 50k calls / month (avg 4k tokens/call).

Key questions for the proposal:
- How do you count tokens for embeddings vs chat (per-request vs per-token rounding)?
- Do you support volume slabs with monthly commit tiers and a separate multiplier for premium models?
- Can committed volume roll over month-to-month? If so, how many months?
- What are overage rates and is there a per-token cap for billing purposes?

I've attached our procurement requirements (BL-procurement-requirements.pdf) — happy to jump on a quick call if it helps. We are targeting a decision by the end of November.

Jordan (procurement) is looped on this thread.

Best,
Alex Miller
Head of Platform
BlueLantern Analytics
[Attachment: BL-procurement-requirements.pdf (pdf)]
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex@bluelantern.ai>
Cc: Jordan Li <procurement@bluelantern.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ask — commit tiers, model premiums, embeddings pricing

Hi Alex / Jordan,

Appreciate the detail — attaching a starter slab model (Pricing_Slab_v3.xlsx) and a one-page draft pricing memo (Draft_MA_Pricing.pdf). Below is a short summary to get us aligned; I'll follow up with a formal quote once we agree on the commit length and token-counting rules.

Starter pricing summary (hosted API, per-token):
- No commit (on-demand): $0.00160 per 1k input tokens, $0.00240 per 1k output tokens (standard chat models).
- Commit tiers (monthly billed as committed tokens):
  - 0.5–2B tokens/month: 12% discount off on-demand
  - 2–5B tokens/month: 18% discount
  - 5B+ tokens/month: 25% discount
- Premium model multiplier: default 1.6x of the per-token rate for premium family (chat-lg-premium).
- Embeddings: listed at 0.5x of chat per-token cost by default, counted per-token with per-request rounding up to 1 token.
- Overage: billed at on-demand rates (no extra multiplier) unless a negotiated overage cap is specified.
- Rollover: up to one full monthly commit may be rolled into the following month for 6+ month commits.

Open items we need from you to finalize: expected month-by-month token profile (used to size the slab), preferred commit length (6 vs 12 months), and whether you want the premium models unbundled (line-item on invoice) or baked into a blended per-token rate.

If it helps, we can reduce the premium multiplier for embeddings-heavy workflows or provide a separate embeddings SKU.

Next steps: I'll draft a formal quote once you confirm commit length and the decision on premium model handling.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Pricing_Slab_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: Draft_MA_Pricing.pdf (pdf)]
From: Jordan Li <procurement@bluelantern.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Alex Miller <alex@bluelantern.ai>
Date: 2026-11-14T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ask — commit tiers, model premiums, embeddings pricing

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Couple clarifying points from procurement and engineering:
- For embeddings, our data team tends to do lots of small calls — rounding to 1 token would materially overstate usage. Can you confirm whether embeddings can be billed per-byte or with sub-token granularity?
- For premium models, we prefer a separate line item so we can track premium spend separately for chargeback across teams.
- Rollover: one month is fine, but can we get an option for two-month rollover on a 12-month commit?
- Overages: procurement prefers a negotiated cap (e.g., not to exceed 120% of committed monthly tokens).

Also attaching a short usage sample (inline below):
- Month 1: 1.3B chat input / 1.0B chat output; embeddings 45k calls
- Month 2: 1.6B input / 1.4B output; embeddings 60k calls
- Month 3: expected spike to 2.8B chat tokens by campaign

Would you be able to provide a counter proposal that includes: 6-month and 12-month commit options, a premium model line item, and a two-month rollover option for 12-month?

Jordan Li
Procurement, BlueLantern Analytics
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: FW: BlueLantern pricing — margin check and counter

Karthik / Dev — forwarding the thread and the usage sample from BlueLantern. They want both 6- and 12-month options + two-month rollover on 12-month and a separate premium model line item. High-level ask: they have a near-term spike (month 3) so we should size slabs to avoid huge overage.

Proposed counter (my thinking):
- 6-month commit: blended 10% discount on chat base (after premium multiplier), premium multiplier 1.4x, embeddings SKU at 0.75x of chat per-token, 1-month rollover, 110% overage cap.
- 12-month commit: blended 16% discount on chat base, premium multiplier 1.35x, embeddings at 0.7x, 2-month rollover, 105% overage cap.

Margin impact: with 12-month terms our margin improves ~4–6 pts versus 6-month, but lowering the premium multiplier to 1.35x will compress premium revenue by ~8%. Dev — any constraints on reserving throughput credits to guarantee their latency SLO for the premium family if we offer 1.35x?

Please reply with quick yes/no on the numbers so I can send a formal counter.

Thanks,
Grace
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T11:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FW: BlueLantern pricing — margin check and counter

Grace / Karthik — engineering can support 1.35x for premium models if the deal includes reserved throughput (dedicated capacity credits) sized to the expected peak month. We will need a short lead time (2 weeks) to pin capacity and add a fallback policy (auto-failover to standard family at similar latency for degraded performance). Rollover rules don't affect runtime.

- Dev
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Alex Miller <alex@bluelantern.ai>, Jordan Li <procurement@bluelantern.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T15:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing ask — commit tiers, model premiums, embeddings pricing

Alex / Jordan,

Thanks for the usage sample — based on internal alignment here's a formal counter proposal. I'll attach the updated slab workbook. If this looks good I'll issue a draft quote and SOW.

Counter proposal (hosted API):
- Option A — 6-month commit
  - Committed volume: 2.5B tokens/month (blended expected)
  - Discount: 10% off on-demand chat rates
  - Premium model: separate line item at 1.4x per-token (can be lowered for embeddings-heavy routes)
  - Embeddings SKU: 0.75x of chat per-token cost; billed per-token, we will apply a per-call aggregation rule to avoid per-request rounding penalty (we'll aggregate by hourly bins for small calls).
  - Rollover: 1 month; overage cap: 110% of committed tokens billed at committed rates up to cap, excess billed at on-demand
  - Reserved throughput: optional add-on — recommended to cover month 3 spike.

- Option B — 12-month commit
  - Committed volume: 2.2B tokens/month (blended expected, lower base due to longer term)
  - Discount: 16% off on-demand chat rates
  - Premium model: separate line item at 1.35x per-token
  - Embeddings SKU: 0.70x of chat per-token cost; 2-month rollover; overage cap: 105%
  - Reserved throughput: included for a negotiated band to ensure latency SLO for premium family

Other terms:
- We will not do sub-token billing per request for embeddings. Instead, we'll aggregate embedding calls hourly and round the hourly aggregate to the nearest token to avoid over-counting frequent tiny calls (this reduces the rounding penalty you mentioned).
- We can provide an explicit overage cap (110%/105%) as requested.
- We'll provide a draft invoice layout with premium model as a line item so your chargeback system can allocate costs.

Next steps: tell me whether you prefer Option A or B and if we should include reserved throughput for month 3. I'll prepare a formal quote and SOW for signature.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Pricing_Slab_v3.xlsx (updated) (spreadsheet)]
